newsitem.title: USA: Fidelity Magellan raised stock holdings in March.
newsitem.headline: Fidelity Magellan raised stock holdings in March.

text.p: Fidelity Investments said on Monday its massive Magellan Fund raised its holdings in stocks to 96.4 percent of assets at the end of March versus 95.5 percent at the end of February.
According to Fidelity's website, Magellan's holdings in cash and other assets at the end of March were 3.5 percent of assets, down from 4.5 percent at the end of February.
Bond holdings remained at zero, and 0.1 percent of assets were invested in convertibles at the end of March, the most recent date figures available, up from zero at the end of February.

According to data appearing on the Website, holdings in energy shares rose to 14.0 percent of assets at the end of March from 13.1 percent at the end of February. Technology shares slipped slightly to 13.7 percent from 13.8 percent, financial stocks rose to 10.6 percent from 10.5 percent, industrial machinery and equipment rose to 8.4 percent from 7.9 percent and healthcare companies rose to 7.8 percent from 7.3 percent.
Durables fell to 8.1 percent of assets from 8.8 percent.
An up-to-date list of Magellan's top 10 holdings and its total assets as of the end of April was unavailable.

At the end of February, its top 10 holdings were General Electric Co, Intel Corp, Philip Morris Cos Inc, CSX Corp, Chrysler Corp, Citicorp, Schlumberger Ltd, Merck & Co Inc, Exxon Corp and American International Group Inc.
Total assets in Magellan were $51.4 billion at the end of March compared to $53.8 billion at the end of February, according to the Fidelity monthly mutual fund guide.
